title: Codimension induction for finite ordinary resolution approximations
statement:
Let $\mathscr C$ be the category of reduced Noetherian quasi-excellent schemes over $\mathbf Q$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-exc-excellent-ring], including finite disjoint unions, with all regular morphisms. Here Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings, quasi-excellence means quasi-excellence of affine coordinate rings, and regular means flat with geometrically regular fibres. Fix a rule $H$ on Cartier-divisor pairs having exactly the properties stated in [lem-per-small-singular-locus-resolution].

For $x\in X\in\mathscr C$, put $c_X(x)=\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$, the supremum of lengths of prime chains in the local ring, and $X^{\le d}=\{x:c_X(x)\le d\}$. An ordinary blowup tower has coherent ideal centers and retains their scheme structures [def-nagata-global-blowup, pqf-def-coherent]. Its unresolved set $T(R)$ is the union in $X$ of the image of the singular locus of its terminal scheme and the images of the singular loci of all its centers; singular means not regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Such a tower is resolved through codimension $d$ if $T(R)$ is closed and disjoint from $X^{\le d}$. Call a center equicodimensional over $X$ if its image has pure codimension $e$ for one $e$ (every generic point of that image has $c_X=e$), and the inverse image of those generic points is schematically dense in the center, meaning that no proper closed subscheme of the center contains that inverse image.

There is a compatible construction, from $H$, of finite prefixes $R_0,\ldots,R_d$ of rules for every $d\ge0$, with the following properties. $R_0(X)$ is the tower of length zero. Each $R_d(X)$ is a finite tower on reduced Noetherian quasi-excellent schemes, all of whose centers are nonempty, reduced, nowhere dense and equicodimensional over $X$ with codimension at most $d$, and it is resolved through codimension $d$. For every regular $f:Y\to X$, $R_d(Y)$ is the contracted scheme-theoretic pullback of $R_d(X)$: only empty centers are deleted and the other extended ideal sheaves are retained in order. Write $T_d(X)=T(R_d(X))$. For $e\ge d$ the sets $T_e(X)$ are contained in $T_d(X)$, and over $X\setminus T_d(X)$ the towers $R_e(X)$ and $R_d(X)$ agree after removal of empty centers, with their ordered center ideals. Any center of $R_e(X)$ of $X$-codimension greater than $d$ lies over $T_d(X)$.

The prefix of length zero exists as specified, and each prefix already constructed by this construction has a successor with the same properties, without changing any earlier rule. In particular the compatible prefixes determine one sequence $(R_d)_{d\ge0}$. This assertion does not claim that this sequence stabilizes or that any $R_d(X)$ is globally resolved.

source.place: §§4.1.1--4.1.5 and the construction in §4.3, printed pp.26--31: finite codimension approximations and their successor construction (before the stabilization argument of Lemma 4.1.3(ii)); Temkin, arXiv:0904.1592v2, read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this desingularization result. ILO VIII 2.3.9--2.3.11 identifies this as the input for its Theorem 2.3.10.

proof.text: We construct rules by induction on $d$, simultaneously retaining the stronger invariant that every center is supported over $X_{\mathrm{sing}}$. Start with $R_0(X)$ empty. A height-zero local ring of a reduced Noetherian scheme is a field (its maximal ideal is its nilradical), so $T_0(X)=X_{\mathrm{sing}}$ misses $X^{\le0}$ and is closed by [lem-per-regular-pullback-unresolved-strata]. The empty tower is preserved under every pullback. At every later stage this same cited closedness assertion applies. The induction below only calls already defined rules $R_i$ with $i\le d$ on further objects, so it does not change any earlier rule.

source.place: §4.3, start of the proof; §§4.1.1--4.1.2; agent-written local/schematic-closure formulation of the codimension induction

proof.text: Suppose the rules through $d$ are constructed, and set $r=d+1$, $f=R_d(X)$ and $Z=T_d(X)$. By [lem-per-regular-pullback-unresolved-strata], the height-$r$ points of $Z$ form a finite set $S$ of generic points. If $S$ is empty set $R_r(X)=f$. Otherwise let $C=\overline S_{\mathrm{red}}$ and $U=X\setminus C$. The set $C$ lies in $Z$, has pure codimension $r$, and its local scheme at each $s\in S$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$; hence $C$ is regular at these points. Insert $\operatorname{Bl}_C(X)\to X$ at the start of $f$ using [lem-per-blowup-sequence-insertion]. Each old center has image of pure codimension at most $d$, so its generic image points avoid $C$; its assumed schematic density over those points makes it the closure of its restriction over $U$. This verifies the insertion hypothesis. Every old replacement retains its reduced structure, pure image codimension and schematic density, by the same node.

source.place: §4.3, Extension 0; agent-written local/schematic-closure formulation of the codimension induction

proof.text: The pullback of the ideal of $C$ to the new first stage is an effective Cartier ideal by [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center], and it stays so through every subsequent blowup by [lemma-nagata-cartier-total-transform-blowup]. All ambient schemes are reduced Noetherian by [lem-per-blowup-local-dimension-bound]; their local schemes and reduced centers are quasi-excellent by its last clause. Properness needed for taking images and globalizing follows at every blowup from [thm-nagata-global-blowup-proper]. Thus all local objects used below belong to $\mathscr C$. Over $U$ the inserted stages are empty and the old tower, including its ideals, is unchanged. Over $X^{\le d}$ the same holds, since $C$ has no such points.

source.place: §4.3, Extension 0 and Lemma 4.3.1; agent-written local/schematic-closure formulation of the codimension induction

proof.text: Process the old centers in their original order, after the new first center. If $W\subset P$ is the current old center, put $W_S=\coprod_{s\in S}(W\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,s})$. By [lem-per-blowup-local-dimension-bound], every summand has dimension at most $r-1=d$. Consequently the already constructed $R_d(W_S)$ is a complete strong resolution: its unresolved set is disjoint from every point. Moreover $W_S$ is regular away from its closed base fibres: at a proper generalization of $s$ the image has height less than $r$, where the old tower was already strongly resolved and all our insertions are empty. By the stronger inductive invariant, every center of $R_d(W_S)$ is therefore supported over those closed fibres. Apply [lem-per-local-blowup-tower-globalization] with $P=W$ to its synchronized centers, blowing them up in the ambient scheme containing $W$. Its conclusion identifies the local strict transforms with the terminal scheme of $R_d(W_S)$, so the new strict transform of $W$ is regular over every $s\in S$. The inserted centers themselves are regular there. Each global new center is reduced, nowhere dense and equicodimensional over $X$ of codimension $r$.

source.place: §4.3, Extensions 1,...,n; localization at the selected points before pushing centers forward; agent-written local/schematic-closure formulation of the codimension induction

proof.text: Insert the ambient correction just obtained before the blowup in $W$, using [lem-per-blowup-sequence-insertion]. Its first replaced center is precisely the strict transform of $W$ just resolved locally. Every still-later old center is schematically dense away from $C$, because its generic image codimension is at most $d<r$, so the remaining insertion hypotheses hold. The previous old centers and previous inserted centers occur before this correction and are unchanged. There are only finitely many original centers; processing each exactly once therefore ends with a finite tower all of whose centers are regular over $X^{\le r}$. All correction centers lie over $C\subset Z$; they lie over $X_{\mathrm{sing}}$ as well, since by the stronger invariant $f$ is the identity over $X_{\mathrm{reg}}$, whence $Z\subset X_{\mathrm{sing}}$. This preserves singular support. It also shows that these corrections are empty on $X\setminus Z$.

source.place: §4.3, Extensions 1,...,n; termination by the finite list of old centers; agent-written local/schematic-closure formulation of the codimension induction

proof.text: Let $P$ be the terminal scheme after these corrections. For $s\in S$ put $P_s=P\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,s}$ and let $D_s$ be the scheme-theoretic inverse image of the reduced point $s$. It is an effective Cartier divisor by the persistence of the ideal of $C$ proved above. Since $P\to X$ is proper and of finite type, $D_s$ is of finite type over $\kappa(s)$, a characteristic-zero field. The singular locus of $P_s$ is contained in $D_s$: outside the closed fibre the image has height at most $d$ and all modifications made there are the old, already resolved tower. Apply the given rule of [lem-per-small-singular-locus-resolution] once to the finite disjoint union $(\coprod P_s,\coprod D_s)$. This gives one finite ordered list of regular centers and a regular terminal scheme on each component, with synchronizing empty stages allowed. Each center is supported over the closed fibres, because that rule supports centers over the singular locus. All its hypotheses, including reducedness and quasi-excellence, were verified above.

source.place: §4.3, final Extension n+1: the simultaneous Cartier-divisor pairs; agent-written local/schematic-closure formulation of the codimension induction

proof.text: Append the globalization of this last tower to $P$, using [lem-per-local-blowup-tower-globalization]. Call the resulting tower $R_r(X)$. Its new centers have pure $X$-codimension $r$, are reduced and nowhere dense, and are schematically dense over their generic image points. The local centers and terminal scheme are regular over all $s\in S$. Outside $C$ the new stages are empty. Thus the terminal scheme and every center are regular over all of $X^{\le r}$: over a height-$r$ point not in $Z$ the old tower was already resolved; the only height-$r$ points of $C$ are $S$; lower heights are unaffected. Closedness from [lem-per-regular-pullback-unresolved-strata] now gives $T_r(X)\cap X^{\le r}=\varnothing$. All new centers lie over $C\subset Z$ and therefore the old tower is unchanged, with its ordered ideals, over $X\setminus Z$.

source.place: §4.3, final Extension and the verification of resolution through codimension r; agent-written local/schematic-closure formulation of the codimension induction

proof.text: Let $h:Y\to X$ be regular. By [lem-per-regular-pullback-unresolved-strata], the selected finite set for $Y$ consists of the generic points above $S$, and its reduced closure is exactly $C\times_XY$; the local maps at these points are regular. This proves compatibility of the first blowup. At each old center, its local disjoint union on $Y$ maps regularly to the local disjoint union on $X$. Inductive functoriality of $R_d$ gives the same synchronized correction list after pullback and deletion of empty centers. Globalization and insertion commute with flat base change by [lem-per-local-blowup-tower-globalization] and [lem-per-blowup-sequence-insertion]. At the terminal correction the local maps are regular in the cited pair category: they are flat with geometrically regular fibres, so their fibres remain regular after each finite extension of a target residue field. The divisor is the schematic pullback of the same ideal of $C$. Thus these are morphisms of $\mathscr P$, and functoriality of the given $H$ in [lem-per-small-singular-locus-resolution] applies. It yields the same conclusion for the final list. An old center that disappears has an empty local correction too; its whole block disappears. These observations preserve the original relative order of every surviving ideal. They also cover the case where the selected set on $Y$ is empty. Hence $R_r(Y)$ is exactly the contracted scheme-theoretic pullback of $R_r(X)$.

source.place: §4.3, functoriality paragraph; simultaneous disjoint-union ordering; agent-written local/schematic-closure formulation of the codimension induction

proof.text: No stage of this construction changes $R_i$ for $i<r$. At the successor just built every inserted center has codimension $r$ and lies over $T_d(X)$, and all old centers are recovered off that set by their closure prescription. Since the tower remains strongly resolved on $X\setminus T_d(X)$, its unresolved set satisfies $T_r(X)\subseteq T_d(X)$. Iterate these inclusions. For $e\ge d$, each later inserted center is supported over the corresponding unresolved set, hence over $T_d(X)$; the same is true of its later strict transforms. The repeated closure replacements of old centers agree off $T_d(X)$, so $R_e(X)$ restricts there to $R_d(X)$ with only empty centers removed and all surviving ideals in order. Every center of codimension greater than $d$ was inserted at one of those later stages, so has the required support. Induction on the natural numbers, starting at the specified empty rule and using only previously fixed rules and $H$, defines one compatible sequence. No stabilization or finite bound on $\dim X$ is used.

source.place: §4.1.5, the support condition before the stabilization argument; finite induction; agent-written local/schematic-closure formulation of the codimension induction
